_fixture.note: Hand-authored HTML for the M002.4 extraction boundary. No page was captured from a live origin, no bytes came off the wire, and every host is a reserved non-resolvable name (example.invalid). Bodies that must carry bytes JSON cannot hold as text are base64 encoded and labelled body_base64.

cases.why: The ordinary case: headings establish attribution, block elements establish runs, script/style/comment content never reaches the text, and entities are decoded once.

cases.why: A document that is nothing but headings is still readable text, so a heading is emitted as its own block rather than only as attribution.
Named and numeric references resolve; an unknown reference stays as the text a reader sees; a double-escaped reference is not decoded twice; a non-breaking space becomes an ordinary space.
When the header declares no character set, the document's own <meta> declaration decides, so a Latin-1 body is read as Latin-1 instead of being refused or mojibake'd.
XHTML is an HTML document for this extractor, and a redirect stays visible: the requested URL and the final URL are both kept on the extracted page.

expected.text:
Note

XHTML parses like HTML here.

cases.why: A recorded loss, not a claim: whitespace inside <pre> is collapsed like any other run, so preformatted layout is not preserved. The case exists so the limitation is data rather than folklore.
An empty heading is not a heading change: text that follows it stays attributed to the last heading a reader actually saw.

refusals.why: An empty body is a fact about the response, not a page with no words.
A body of nothing but whitespace is the same fact as an empty body.
A PDF is refused rather than half-parsed as text; PDF extraction is a separate boundary that does not exist yet.
refusals.expected_reason_contains: which is not an HTML document

refusals.why: The declared type is authoritative: markup served as text/plain is still not an HTML document.
refusals.expected_reason_contains: which is not an HTML document

refusals.why: A response that declares no media type cannot be assumed to be HTML.
refusals.expected_reason_contains: which is not an HTML document

refusals.why: The extraction ceiling is separate from the acquisition ceiling and refuses the document instead of truncating it.
Markup that cannot be read is refused rather than guessed at.
An unclosed comment would silently swallow the rest of the document.
An unclosed script element would swallow the rest of the document, so it is a markup failure rather than a page with no text.
refusals.expected_reason_contains: an unclosed <script> element swallowed the rest of the document

refusals.why: An unclosed title element swallows the body the same way an unclosed script does.
refusals.expected_reason_contains: an unclosed <title> element swallowed the rest of the document

refusals.why: A NUL byte means the body is not the text it claims to be.
refusals.expected_reason_contains: the body contained a NUL byte

refusals.why: A body with no markup at all is not an HTML document this extractor can attest to.
Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 are refused rather than replaced with lossy characters.
refusals.expected_reason_contains: the body was not valid utf-8

refusals.why: Markup with a title and nothing else readable is a typed outcome, not an empty page.
A declared character set this extractor does not decode is refused rather than decoded as something else.
refusals.expected_reason_contains: declared the unsupported character set shift_jis

refusals.why: A document that declares an undecodable character set is refused on the document's own statement, not only on the header's.
refusals.expected_reason_contains: declared the unsupported character set windows-1252

refusals.why: A snapshot that cannot name its source could never be cited, so extraction refuses before producing one.
